I would wait for evidence of a bottom before buying: ETF flows stabilising, or price recovering levels like $65K, or a Fed that sounds less likely to keep hiking. US spot BTC ETF outflows in November reached about $5.4B, the largest monthly outflow on record; ETH ETFs had eight straight days of outflows
Markets price about a 93-98% chance of a 25bp Fed hike on Dec 9; Fed minutes point to more hikes, with inflation around 3.8%

ETH/BTC ratio is around 0.028; ETH is down more than 40% this year, with falling fee revenue and Solana overtaking it in DEX volume
Democratic midterm sweep raises the risk of tighter crypto regulation; a tech stock sell-off (including Nvidia CEO's resignation) is adding to risk-off pressure
output.rationale: The trend and macro picture both point down, so I'm keeping most of the portfolio in cash and taking only a small BTC position. Momentum is clearly negative. BTC is down 25% over the past month and has fallen for eight weeks in a row. It is now below its 200-week moving average (about $68k), a long-term trend line it has rarely traded under. ETH is weaker on every timeframe, and its price relative to BTC keeps falling. The macro backdrop is also tightening. Prediction markets put the odds of a Fed rate hike on Dec 9 at about 93% or higher. Fed minutes point to further hikes into 2027, inflation is running around 3.8%, and the 10-year Treasury yield was reported at about 5.1% in mid-November. US spot BTC ETFs have had their largest monthly outflows on record, over $5B in November, and ETH ETFs have also seen steady redemptions. After the Democratic midterm sweep, tighter crypto regulation is also a risk. On the other side, there are signs of capitulation that usually come before rebounds over a horizon of several months. The Fear & Greed index is at 10-13, about half of all BTC supply is held at a loss, K33 reported deeply oversold daily RSI readings, and leverage has been heavily cleared out through repeated liquidations of $1-2B. History suggests breaks below the 200-week average tend to reverse, but some analysts (Wintermute, Benjamin Cowen) warn BTC could fall to $40-50k. Because the evidence is mixed and the main macro catalyst is still to come, I'm taking a starter position of 15% in BTC only. That gives some exposure to a mean-reversion rebound while limiting losses if the bear market continues. I'm skipping ETH because of its higher volatility (50% vs 40%), weaker relative strength, falling fee revenue and persistent ETF outflows. I'll add more only if price or ETF flows stabilize, for example BTC reclaiming $68-70k or ETF outflows ending. This reflects my reading of current news, not a confident call on the bottom.
